title: Local correction from a nearby dictator
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ map the sign cube of dimension $2^n$ to the signs $\{-1,1\}$, and choose coordinates $j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and $i\in\{0,\ldots,2^n-1\}$. Let $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, and suppose the fraction of inputs on which $f$ differs from the dictator reading coordinate $i$ is at most $0.2\varepsilon$. For a uniformly random $y$ in the binary cube of dimension $2^n$, convert $f$ to a sign-valued function $g$ on that binary cube using the coordinatewise identification of bits with signs, and let $a$ be the sign string whose entry at a binary string $z$ is the sign corresponding to bit $j$ of $z$. Then the probability that $g(y)g(y+a)$ equals the sign corresponding to bit $j$ of the binary string indexed by $i$ is at least $1-0.4\varepsilon$ and at least $1/2$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the dimension-$2^n$ sign cube to $\{-1,1\}$
Relative Hamming distance from $f$ to the dictator at coordinate $i$ is at most $200(1/1000)\varepsilon$
